correctness.rationale: Define q from oriented Γ one-cube [u,v] (distinct supported pair) to oriented simplicial edge [u,v]. Its kernel is the free group spanned by reverse-edge sums, each a valid Γ-square boundary ∂(u,v,u,u)=[u,v]+[v,u]. For an arbitrary valid Γ square (a,b,c,d), radius-one-ball images at (1,0) and (0,1) give simplicial triangles {a,b,d} and {a,c,d}; thus q∂Γ(a,b,c,d)=∂[a,b,d]-∂[a,c,d]. Conversely each simplicial triangle {a,b,c} within a hyperedge lifts as the admissible square (a,b,a,c), whose Γ boundary maps to ∂[a,b,c]. These inclusions yield q(im∂Γ2)=im∂simp2 and ker q⊂im∂Γ2, a canonical quotient-chain isomorphism compatible with zero-degree boundary and hypergraph vertex maps. The known 6-vertex 10-triangle RP2 has integral H1=Z/2, and any f.g. abelian group is H1 of some finite triangulated 2-complex; choose its maximal simplices as hyperedges. Scope only degrees 0/1 and supported vertices; sample HNF checks cannot extrapolate but the explicit chain argument is universal.

The mathematical content is the all-hypergraph chain-relation theorem, not the textbook RP2 torsion table.

final_claim: For any finite hypergraph with all vertices supported by nonempty hyperedges, the normalized radius-one-ball Γ-cubical homology of Zaidi–Jamil has natural integral H_i^Γ(H;Z)≅H_i(K(H);Z) for i=0,1, where K(H) is downward-closure simplicial complex. In particular a six-vertex RP2 facet hypergraph has first Gamma homology Z/2 and every finitely generated abelian group is realizable in first Γ-homology.
